item.title: Oral Obesity Drugs
item.description:
• Summary: A deep dive into the competitive landscape of oral obesity drugs, examining emerging oral GLP-1 receptor agonists and other non-injectable therapies. The article compares efficacy, safety profiles, and market potential as companies race to capture a share of the growing obesity treatment market.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: BioSpace

item.title: AstraZeneca FDA Approval for Hypertension Drug (Baxdrostat/Baxfendy)
item.description:
• Summary: The FDA granted approval to AstraZeneca's baxdrostat (brand name Baxfendy) for hypertension, representing a first‑in‑class aldosterone synthase inhibitor. The approval marks a new class of blood‑pressure medicines for patients who do not achieve adequate control with existing therapies. In a related regulatory action, the FDA also approved Fasenra (benralizumab) for a new indication, though the primary focus remains on baxdrostat's landmark nod.
  • MoAs: Aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) inhibitor; reduces aldosterone production, thereby lowering blood pressure by decreasing sodium retention and vascular resistance.
  • Sources: STAT News, Fierce Pharma, BioPharma Dive, BioSpace, Endpoints News

item.title: Vincentage Oral GLP-1 Obesity Results
item.description:
• Summary: Vincentage reported 12.4% weight loss from its oral GLP-1 receptor agonist in a clinical trial, positioning it to compete with Eli Lilly's drugs in the Chinese market.
  • MoAs: GLP-1 receptor agonist
  • Sources: Fierce Biotech
